key_insight: Human experts and LLMs performed similarly in proposing synthesis recipes, and their closed-loop collaboration enabled discovery of a new material prototype, Ba3PtO5.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that AI can accelerate materials synthesis planning when paired with experimental validation, making it a practical workflow for discovering new compounds in complex chemical spaces.
method: Generated synthesis recipes for known and unknown Ruddlesden-Popper-related materials using both humans and LLMs.
Tested proposed recipes experimentally in the lab and fed outcomes back into a closed-loop iteration.
Compared performance across two rounds to assess how collaboration affects synthesis success.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparable success rates for humans and LLMs across rounds, including strong performance on known materials and much lower success on unknown targets.
watch_item: Success on known compounds does not guarantee reliable discovery of novel materials, so experimental validation and careful target selection remain essential.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
